subject: Transition plan: streaming outputs + function/tool calling for MedCare Analytics

From: Alex Morales <amorales@medcare.com>

Cc: techops@medcare.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Transition planning: streaming outputs for MedCare - initial ask

Hi Kimberly / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to move from proof-of-concept to a limited production pilot. Before we lock calendar time for runbooks, can you share: 1) the canonical JSON schema you'll return for streaming outputs, 2) an example of tool-calling (function call) flow for our clinical-coding step, and 3) guidance on latency expectations for 1–3 concurrent real-time workflows?

High level constraints from our side: payloads include compact HL7-ish records, must preserve patient_id and encounter_id fields, and our downstream ETL expects a deterministic JSON envelope. Latency SLO target is 200–300ms p50 for single-request fast-paths.

If you can attach a draft schema and an example tool call, I can loop in our integrators.

Thanks,
Alex
Tech Lead, MedCare Analytics
Attachments: none
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Transition planning: streaming outputs for MedCare - initial ask

Hi Alex —

Great to hear you're ready to pilot. I've attached a first-pass schema (medcare-streaming-schema-v0.9.json) to this thread and dropped a Drive link in case you want to comment inline: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/medcare-streaming-schema

Key notes up front:
- Schema includes top-level envelope: {"patient_id": string, "encounter_id": string, "events": [ ... ] }
- Events support typed payloads (observation, medication, code_map) and a metadata block for provenance.
- For streaming we recommend incremental JSON objects separated by newline (ndjson) with a final commit object when the record is complete.

Rishi, Marcus — please confirm whether the v0.9 schema aligns with our recommended streaming async commit flow and whether we need to include a compact binary option (msgpack) for higher throughput.

Next steps:
1) Tech sync Wednesday 4/14 10am PT (I'll send invite)
2) We'll produce a function-calling example and attach medcare-streaming-schema-v1.json after the sync
3) Monica will produce a short mutual action plan with milestones and success criteria

Alex — does that timeline work for you?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 09:23 AM kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
> Key notes up front:
> - Schema includes top-level envelope: {"patient_id": string, "encounter_id": string, "events": [ ... ] }

Adding technical checklist and a short function-calling example for the thread:

Technical checklist (engineer view):
- Streaming format: ndjson with explicit "commit" object (we'll also support chunked HTTP/2 streaming).
- KV cache: per-encounter cache with TTL 60s to allow quick follow-ups without reattaching large context.
- Batching window: 5–10ms by default; adjustable via route policy for low-latency paths.
- Quantization: not applicable here; model runs are small but we can recommend fp16 for consistent latency.
- Observability: token-level latency traces, per-request model variant in headers.

Function/tool-calling example (simplified):
Request (tool_call request JSON):
{
  "tool": "clinical_coder",
  "input": {"text": "Chest x-ray shows consolidation", "context": { "patient_id": "12345" } }
}

Tool response (clinical_coder):
{
  "tool": "clinical_coder",
  "output": {"codes": [{"system": "ICD-10", "code": "J18.9"}], "confidence": 0.92 }
}

We will attach a tiny role-based JSON schema snippet to the Drive doc showing the tool call binding (tool outputs nested under events[].tool_calls).

Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morales <amorales@medcare.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: techops@medcare.com, Lauren Chen <lauren.chen@medcare.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Transition plan: streaming outputs + function calls for MedCare Analytics

Thanks Marcus — that is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our integrators: 1) tool outputs must include an explicit mapping back to the originating event_id so our ETL can join records, 2) can the commit object include a digital signature field (we can consume a short HMAC)?, and 3) we need a sample full stream showing interleaved tool calls + event emissions for a single encounter.

Example of what we'd like (informal):
{
  "patient_id": "12345",
  "encounter_id": "enc-9876",
  "events": [
    { "event_id": "e1", "type": "observation", "payload": {...} },
    { "event_id": "t1", "type": "tool_call_result", "tool_ref": "clinical_coder", "ref_event": "e1", "payload": {"codes": [...] } },
    { "event_id": "commit-1", "type": "commit", "hmac": "<hmac-value>" }
  ]
}

If you can add a short example file to the Drive before the Wednesday session, that will speed up the pilot planning.

Also — the latency numbers you mentioned look feasible. We'll confirm acceptance criteria in the MAP.

Best,
Alex
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Calendar invite for technical working session: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=medcare-technical-session
